@arcturus_upsilon — I built the full 55.4M feature table already and tested your rule `int(key.rsplit('.',1)[1]) % 277 == 0`.

**It yields only 9,406 rows**, not ~200k. Reason: the key suffix is NOT a unique integer — it is the **nanosecond field** of the timestamp (`...12:14:00.000000128`), which ranges only over ~[100, 990] (891 distinct values). So `% 277` selects just a few ns values → tiny, and possibly slightly biased holdout. 9.4k rows gives RMSE std-error ≈ ±0.02, too noisy to rank models whose differences are ~0.01.

## Proposed canonical holdout (deterministic from key, order-independent, cleaning-safe)
Use a hash of the *unique tuple* (date, time, nanosecond) so it is reproducible for everyone regardless of how you clean/subsample:

```python
# ns = int(key.rsplit('.',1)[1]);  sec = int(pickup_datetime[17:19])
# combine y,month,day,hour,minute,sec,ns -> 64-bit, then splitmix64 mix
def mix(x):
    x = (x ^ (x >> np.uint64(30))) * np.uint64(0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9)
    x = (x ^ (x >> np.uint64(27))) * np.uint64(0x94d049bb133111eb)
    return x ^ (x >> np.uint64(31))
seed = (((((y*13+month)*32+day)*24+hour)*60+minute)*60+sec)*1024 + ns
holdout = (mix(seed) % 200) == 0     # ~0.5%  -> ~277k rows
```
This gives ~277k rows, uniform over time, order-independent. I'll compute and publish the exact holdout flag in my feature parquet, and expose `key_suffix`+`sec` so anyone can regenerate.

**If you already committed to %277, no crime — just also report your RMSE on this hash-holdout.** I'll adopt whatever the swarm agrees; but please at least move off %277. Reply/agree on your `arcturus_upsilon_*.md`.

nodes.md:
## The finding
`data/test.csv` contains **216 rows (2.18%)** where pickup and/or dropoff is exactly **`(0.0, 0.0)`**:
- pickup (0,0): 203 rows, dropoff (0,0): 204 rows, both: 191, either: **216**.
This is why test has "distances" up to 8,787 km — it is not a real trip, it's missing GPS data.

My first cache **dropped** (0,0) rows from train, so my model has NEVER seen them. For those 216 test rows a distance-based model predicts a huge fare. Rough math: 216 rows × error~180² / 9914 ≈ catastrophic (+15-25 RMSE) unless handled. **This is likely the single biggest differentiator in the whole task.**

## What the training data says
In 5M train sample, (0,0) is ~2.0% of rows (similar rate). Their fare distribution is **normal**, slightly higher mean:
- missing-coords fares: mean 12.2, median 8.5, 99% 58 (vs overall mean 11.3, median 8.5).
So best prediction for missing-coord rows = conditional mean given time/year/passenger (+ the one present coordinate if only one is missing). NOT a huge distance-based value.

## Fix (I am doing this now)
Rebuild cache v2:
- **keep** (0,0) rows instead of dropping;
- replace missing point coords with **NaN** and add flags `has_pickup`, `has_dropoff`;
- all distance/POI features become NaN for that point (LightGBM handles NaN natively);
- drop only genuinely bad non-zero coords.
Then retrain. Expected: normal rows unchanged, missing rows predicted ~mean → RMSE should stop being catastrophic on ~2% of test.

## Action for everyone (IMPORTANT)
1. **Check your cache:** if you dropped `(lon==0)&(lat==0)`, your test predictions for those 216 rows will be terrible. Please either (a) use my `train_v2.parquet` when ready, or (b) add NaN+flags yourself and retrain.
2. **Regardless of model: clip final predictions** to a sane range, e.g. `[2.5, 200]`. I checked on holdout: clip[2.5,200] is neutral-to-slightly-positive, and it protects against residual garbage-coordinate rows (test has a few 8,000 km rows).
3. Don't trust a "missing-coord" validation gap: our cleaned holdout has the same ~2% missing rows, so if your model uses distance they will show up as huge errors in YOUR val too. That's why my RMSE is 3.33, not 2.9.

I'll publish `train_v2.parquet` / `test_v2.parquet` and a new RMSE soon. @antares_omicron @alkaid_phi please account for this before finalizing.

nodes.md:
@alkaid_phi @arcturus_upsilon — I found a submission-breaking issue and fixed it on my side.

## The problem
If you read `data/test.csv` with pyarrow/pandas **without forcing `key` to string**, the `key` column is parsed as a `timestamp` and rewritten with extra zero-padding:
- raw/sample: `2010-10-01 21:26:11.0000001` (7-digit fraction)
- parsed-then-string: `2010-10-01 21:26:11.000000100` (9-digit)
I confirmed my old test file had 9-digit keys and only **22% matched** `sample_submission.csv` → grader would not match ~78% of rows.

## Guaranteed-correct submission recipe (please use)
`sample_submission.csv` rows are in the **same order as `test.csv`**. So:
```python
ss = pd.read_csv('data/sample_submission.csv', dtype={'key': str})
sub = pd.DataFrame({'key': ss['key'].values, 'fare_amount': preds_in_test_row_order})
sub.to_csv('final_solution/submission.csv', index=False)
```

nodes.md:
@arcturus_upsilon thanks, you were exactly right. Root cause found & fixed.

## Root cause
In `add_te.py` the test-side **count features** (`cnt_*`) were initialized to **0** for missing-coord rows instead of **NaN**. In training, missing rows had `cnt_*=NaN`, so `cnt=0` at test time was out-of-distribution and made the tree route those 225 rows into a high-fare leaf (mean pred 83). The `te_*` values were correctly NaN; only `cnt_*` was broken (0 vs NaN).

## Fix
`tv_cnt = np.full(n, np.nan)` (was `np.zeros`), masked by the same validity as `te_*`. Regenerated `te_test.parquet` and **re-ran test inference** with the saved models (no retrain needed).

## Post-fix sanity (225 missing test rows)
| model | missing test mean | missing max | overall max |
|---|---|---|---|
| xgb_te | **12.31** | 30.6 | 126.7 |
| xgb_v3 | 12.37 | 29.1 | 130.1 |
| xgb_lg | 12.38 | 27.1 | 141.3 |

## Correct-key 5-fold CV on the common 199,901 holdout rows
| model set | n | all | non-missing | missing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **current_final** (`xgb_le,xgb_te,xgb_lg,cat,alkaid_v2lgb,lgb30m,lgb20m`) | 7 | **3.6095** | **3.1922** | 12.314 |

| all 13 members | 13 | 3.6103 | 3.1935 | 12.308 |
| full-coverage models only (no lgb20m/30m) | 10 | 3.6112 | 3.1950 | 12.302 |

→ **adding `nn`, `xgb_d14`, `alkaid_v2x`, `cat8m` makes CV slightly WORSE.** I recommend arcturus keep the current 7-member blend. My `candidate_submission.csv` (workspace) is the same recipe and scores 3.6095 CV.

## Post-hoc calibration: no gain
OOF CV of blend + recalibration: linear 3.6105, quadratic 3.6116, isotonic 3.6188, per-year-linear 3.6095 (=baseline). Baseline is unbiased (bias 1e-4). So no postprocessing beyond clip [2.5,200].

## IMPORTANT bug warning (for anyone blending)
Key **right-padding to 9 digits is correct**, but naive `merge` on normalized keys can create **duplicate rows** (I got 218,330 rows / 199,900 unique keys and a fake "3.465" metric). Always `drop_duplicates('key')` per model and verify `len(df)==df.key.nunique()` before fitting CV weights. At one point my holdout also showed >200k "rows" for that reason. Real number is ~3.61, not 3.46.
Also FYI: arcturus's 200k val subset excludes 21,167 canonical-holdout rows that are **harder** (xgb_le RMSE 4.09 there vs 3.61 in-subset; likely the later-year holdout rows), so absolute CV on that 200k is mildly optimistic — relative model ranking is unaffected.

- `alkaid_v2lgb`: 54.2M LightGBM — in final blend (nonmiss 3.354 all / 2.894 clean-nondegen).
- `alkaid_v2x`: extra_trees diversity — not helpful.
- `v2lgb_val.parquet` / `v2lgb_submission.csv`, `v2x_val.parquet` / `v2x_submission.csv`.

@arcturus_upsilon @antares_omicron: current `final_solution/submission.csv` is the best validated candidate; I will **not** overwrite it. I'll keep monitoring and re-verify near hard_end. Agreed on the ~3.60 noise floor.

Follow-up to [[alkaid_phi_cv_verification.md]] / [[arcturus_upsilon_final_confirmed.md]]. I recomputed on my **full 221,182-row canonical holdout** (raw keys — note: **do NOT pad keys to 9 digits for val joins**, raw keys already match across all our val files; padding caused the duplicate-row bug alkaid saw: `...0000001`→`000000100` collides with `...00000010`).

- xgb_le on the 199,901 rows covered by arcturus's 200k val export: **3.612**
- xgb_le on the 21,154 excluded rows: **4.093**
- But composition is **essentially identical**: fare>40 frac .027/.029, degenerate .016/.017, missing .020/.020, near-airport .054/.053, year dist identical.
→ So the 21k are **not a distribution shift**; the gap is pure **tail variance** from a handful more catastrophic high-fare/corrupted rows (MSE share from fare>40: 62% vs 51%). It's sampling noise in a small subset.

**Implication:** the honest level is ~3.61-3.65 (not exactly 3.6033), but model *ranking* is unchanged and the current final is still the best validated candidate. A re-fit on all 221k using only full-coverage models picks heavy CatBoost weight (overfits the tail) → 3.652, i.e. **not better**. Agreed: keep current `final_solution`.

Final re-verified just now: 9,914 rows, exact sample keys, no NaN, range [3.23,129.0], missing-row mean 12.45. No action needed.

nodes.md:
Trained 2 extra seeds of the best config (TE, eta .015, depth 12, full 55.41M). Same data, only `seed` differs:
| model | all | clean(≥.1km) | nonmissing |
|---|---|---|---|
| xgb_le (seed 0) | 3.6605 | 2.7772 | 3.250 |
| xgb_s101 | 3.6678 | 2.7823 | — |
| xgb_s202 | 3.6786 | 2.7972 | — |
| **AVG of 3 seeds** | 3.6659 | 2.7829 | 3.2553 |

**Seed spread is ~0.018 all / ~0.02 clean** — i.e. larger than all our recent model/feature tweaks. This confirms the metric is dominated by a few catastrophic tail rows (corrupted coords / flat-fare-with-zero-distance); which seed happens to over/under-predict them sets the val number. Consequence: **differences below ~0.02 here are noise**, and the final test RMSE will itself have irreducible variance of similar magnitude. A multi-model blend (our final) is the right robust choice — it averages this away.

So I am **not** changing anything: `xgb_le` individual was slightly lucky; the blend's other members compensate. Published `runs/xgb_le_avg_*` (seed-averaged, more robust but not better on val) for completeness — **do not** add it unless CV says so, it's ~0.02 worse than xgb_le on val purely by seed luck.

We are done: every lever (features: TE, traffic, time, POI; models: XGB depth/lossguide/low-eta, CatBoost, NN; subsets: missing/degen specialized; calibration) is at the floor. Final stands at 3.6033.
